run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-18T00:56:33Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend is backed by the frontend's own error spans: zero in every 5-minute window ending 00:33:33–00:55:33, then 26.7 per 5m at 00:57:33 rising to 563.75 per 5m at 01:03:33 (still 307 per 5m at 01:07:33) [evidence 67c77f89-9b79-4b3d-bf03-6030316f4411-t0:40c78484-829a-4a69-8089-719010babf7a]. The failing frontend operations are cart and checkout calls (GET/POST /api/cart, POST /api/checkout, grpc CartService/GetCart and AddItem, CheckoutService/PlaceOrder), while /api/data and AdService/GetAds stayed at 0 [evidence 29d7da42-96cd-44ae-b092-a5f0feb2c1d2-t1:1fd21200-4460-4293-ab11-86bc33fe8ccf]. Cart itself has its own error spans on POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart and AddItem [evidence 2eece0f7-71b7-4ed2-a13f-5191b8d1a4b9-t0:77137901-0ed2-4c4f-ae58-cdb4ecb0e631] and logs repeat 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' from 01:00:08 through 01:03:56 [evidence 72605b9f-eea7-4e36-a17a-37ac1e833141-t0:ae5593fb-0c52-4d4b-9543-262734269cb1, d29094cd-6c2e-474f-b01c-c27027fa98ae-t1:242ab757-fdd8-4b68-82d1-d3732fa77492]. Its datastore pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft is in CrashLoopBackOff (ready=false, restartCount 4) with last termination OOMKilled, exitCode 137, at 00:59:32 [evidence cb1c8e34-7b50-47be-b171-f1f5fab7e8fb-t1:6b7e4707-24d3-4f3a-87a9-6d2f2898c5f6], and the valkey-cart Service has no ready endpoint [evidence 8f817772-8bcb-49ee-9234-228e983db2da-t0:56885559-28e1-46c3-b11c-509944f8995c]. In the same minutes a Chaos Mesh Schedule named otel-demo-valkey-memory-stress in namespace chaos-mesh began spawning StressChaos objects whose 'Applied' messages name exactly otel-demo/valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft/valkey-cart, first at 00:55:27 — 66 s before the alert opened [evidence 8026eb49-9349-4b3b-b1b0-88d1ef84be32-t0:cc627a1b-0c02-46f6-ae3f-9576e18e0149, b94532c9-9176-4111-8b03-79cfb952a157-t0:e32d9077-4ec0-4ecc-bb62-f80756703a67]. Supported chain: memory-stress chaos on valkey-cart → OOMKill (container limit memory 10Mi) → cart cannot reach redis → cart and frontend error spans → alert. The conclusion is partial: the fault-applying objects are visible only through events (chaos-mesh CRs are not readable in this Run), so the stress parameters and when the Schedule was created/changed are unknown; the injected memory itself is not visible in container_memory_working_set_bytes samples.

claims.text: frontend's own error spans (traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}) were 0 in every 5m window ending 00:33:33 through 00:55:33, then 26.67 at 00:57:33, 111.11 at 00:59:33, 426.67 at 01:01:33, 563.75 at 01:03:33, 446.50 at 01:05:33 and 307.48 at 01:07:33.

The erroring frontend operations are the cart/checkout path: 9-minute increases at 01:09:00–01:13:00 show GET /api/cart 40.6, POST /api/cart 73.7, POST /api/checkout 22.4, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem 73.7, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart 40.6 and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 22.4, while GET /api/data, grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds and tcp.connect stayed at 0.

The cart service has its own error spans in the 20 minutes ending 01:00:00 — POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem 16.90 and POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart 10.87 — the only cart operations carrying STATUS_CODE_ERROR in that view.

Cart pod cart-755465879b-4p8d9 logs 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' repeatedly from 01:00:08 to 01:01:05, then 'Connection to redis was restored successfully.' and 'Successfully connected to Redis' at 01:01:10, and again 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' from 01:02:38 to 01:03:56.

Pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft is Running but not ready: container valkey-cart is in state waiting reason CrashLoopBackOff ('back-off 1m20s restarting failed container=valkey-cart'), restartCount 4, and lastState terminated with reason OOMKilled, exitCode 137, startedAt 2026-11-18T00:59:21Z finishedAt 2026-11-18T00:59:32Z, containerID containerd://26cfff7d394f2635788cab4b098dfbc9f4e288edf32b37217893d5810340b3d3.

The valkey-cart Deployment declares container valkey-cart with resources limits cpu 10m / memory 10Mi (requests cpu 2m / memory 4Mi) and image valkey/valkey:8.1.3-alpine; its status shows Available=False, reason MinimumReplicasUnavailable, lastTransitionTime 2026-11-18T00:59:32Z. The cart Deployment declares env VALKEY_ADDR=valkey-cart:6379 with limits cpu 45m / memory 165Mi.
The valkey-cart Service endpoint set contains only notReadyAddresses for pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft port 6379, while the cart Service has a ready address for cart-755465879b-4p8d9 port 8080.

A kubelet BackOff Warning event 'Back-off restarting failed container valkey-cart in pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft_otel-demo' occurs 22 times on that pod, firstTimestamp 2026-11-18T00:56:31Z, lastTimestamp 2026-11-18T01:03:49Z.

Chaos Mesh Schedule otel-demo-valkey-memory-stress in namespace chaos-mesh reports Normal 'Spawned'/'Create new object' events for StressChaos objects otel-demo-valkey-memory-stress-flgz4 (00:55:27Z), -ckxt6 (00:56:27Z), -w8p5x (00:57:27Z), -nt6th (00:58:27Z), -95xf6 (00:59:27Z), -v75mv (01:02:17Z) and -psc57 (01:03:12Z), plus Warning 'Forbid spawning new job because: ... is still running' at 01:01:27, 01:02:27, 01:03:12, 01:03:27 and 01:03:40.

Those StressChaos experiments report 'Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft/valkey-cart' at 00:55:27, 00:56:27, 00:57:27, 00:58:27, 00:59:27, 01:02:17 and 01:03:12 (each followed by 'Time up according to the duration' and 'Recovered' about 55 s later), and the later experiments report Warning 'Failed to apply chaos: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = no running task found: task 26cfff7d394f2635788cab4b098dfbc9f4e288edf32b37217893d5810340b3d3 not found' — the same container ID the pod records for its OOMKilled valkey-cart instance.

The frontend and cart pods themselves are up: frontend-675fd7b5c5-x9gbm and cart-755465879b-4p8d9 are phase Running with ready=true, restartCount 0, containers running since 00:18:56Z and 00:19:06Z respectively.

At 60 s sampling the valkey-cart container's own working set (container_memory_working_set_bytes{container="valkey-cart"}) stayed between about 3.4 MB and 3.9 MB from 00:32:33 to 01:06:33, i.e. no sample approached or exceeded the 10Mi limit.
The cart container's working set rose from about 57.7 MB at 00:32:33 to about 103.6 MB at 00:58:33 and 97.8 MB at 01:00:33, remaining below the declared 165Mi limit.

Cart pod log lines sampled in the 00:34–00:42 window (newest 40 of 2820 matching lines, 00:41:55.954Z–00:41:59.999Z) show ordinary handling: 'AddItemAsync called with userId=...', 'GetCartAsync called with userId=...', 'EmptyCartAsync called with userId=...'.

Healthy-looking neighbours: in the 20-minute error-span view ending 01:00:00 the payment error-span series (GET, dns.lookup, tcp.connect), checkout's oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and oteldemo.CartService/GetCart, accounting's 'orders receive', ad's ResolveBoolean and frontend's /api/data path all showed an increase of 0, i.e. these series carried no error spans in that view.

The flagd EventStream error spans in services ad, fraud-detection and recommendation appear as about 1 error per 5-minute period sporadically across the whole window, including periods before 00:55:27, so they are background activity and are not tied to this alert.
A cluster-wide query of kind networkpolicies returned no items (result_count 1, an empty list), so no NetworkPolicy is visible that could explain cart→valkey connection failures.

Frontend errors caused by a rise in request volume is rejected: frontend span volume fell from 13222.2 per 5m at 00:41:33 to 8451.1 at 01:01:33 and 5704.9 at 01:06:33 while error spans rose over the same period.

Crashes or restarts of the frontend or cart containers are rejected as the cause: both pods are Running and ready with restartCount 0, and the cart Service still has a ready endpoint, so the failures reach them from another entity.

Root cause hypothesis: the Chaos Mesh Schedule otel-demo-valkey-memory-stress (namespace chaos-mesh) applies memory stress to the valkey-cart container; with a 10Mi memory limit the container is OOMKilled (exitCode 137 at 00:59:32) and enters CrashLoopBackOff, its Service endpoint becomes notReady-only, the cart service logs 'Wasn't able to connect to redis', and the resulting cart errors surface as frontend /api/cart and /api/checkout error spans that make RequestErrorRate fire.

Contributing configuration hypothesis: the valkey-cart container's 10Mi memory limit leaves little headroom over its observed ~3.4–3.9 MB baseline, so an injected memory stress of any useful size kills it almost immediately.

Read and, if this is not an intended experiment, suspend the Chaos Mesh Schedule otel-demo-valkey-memory-stress in namespace chaos-mesh (and its StressChaos children) before re-testing frontend error rate.
Review the valkey-cart memory limit (10Mi) against the valkey 8.1.3 baseline plus any forking/persistence, and consider raising it so the datastore cannot be OOMKilled by a small external allocation.

gaps: Chaos Mesh CRs are not readable with the available tools: kind Schedule and kind StressChaos are not in the queryable kind list, so the stress parameters (memory size, workers, selector, duration), the Schedule's spec/cron and its creation or last-change time are unknown; the Schedule and its experiments are evidenced only by Kubernetes events.

Events returned by the cluster start at 2026-11-18T00:38:33Z (source_start_at of the events view), so whether otel-demo-valkey-memory-stress spawned experiments before 00:55:27Z — and therefore whether it also explains the pre-00:55 baseline — is unknown.

The declared memory stress is not directly visible in container_memory_working_set_bytes for the valkey-cart container (samples 3.4–3.9 MB at 60 s); the 55 s stress bursts may fall between samples, so the injected allocation itself was not observed.
Valkey-side logs are unavailable: fetch_pod_logs on valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft returned no lines and reported no previous container instance, so no valkey error/OOM log line was observed.
A pod-log query for lines matching 'redis|connect' in cart-755465879b-4p8d9 between 00:19 and 00:45 returned no rows, so whether cart logged Redis failures before 00:45 is unknown.

container_memory_failures_total with scope=container, type=oom for the valkey-cart container returned no series, so the OOM is corroborated only by the container lastState (OOMKilled, exitCode 137) and the chaos events.
Jaeger returned no traces for service frontend in 00:55–01:05, so span-level error messages/status codes behind the error spans are unknown, and no parent-child call edges were observed.

All otel-demo pods, including cart, were (re)started at 00:18–00:20 and the cart ReplicaSet cart-755465879b was created at 00:18:53Z; the earlier ReplicaSet cart-9fd895bb7 no longer exists, so the pod-template change that produced it and its cause are unknown, and it cannot be placed as affected or as changed for another reason.
The exact expression and threshold of the Alertmanager rule RequestErrorRate are unknown: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name RequestErrorRate returned no rules.
The relationship between frontend-proxy's own error spans ('ingress' 89.23 and 'router frontend egress' 19.49 per 20 minutes) and the cart failures was not verified from status codes or error detail.
Downstream or customer impact beyond the otel-demo services was not observed; no change_history integration is available to date when the chaos Schedule or the cart rollout was created.
next_steps: Inspect the chaos-mesh Schedule otel-demo-valkey-memory-stress and its StressChaos children with an API client that can read chaos-mesh CRs (kubectl get schedule,stresschaos -n chaos-mesh -o yaml) to obtain the memory size, workers, duration, selector and schedule, and whether it is still active.
Check chaos-mesh controller logs/older events for spawns of otel-demo-valkey-memory-stress before 00:55:27Z to explain the earlier boundary of the incident.
Consider raising the valkey-cart container memory limit (10Mi) and confirming whether valkey persistence/forking contributed to its memory footprint.
Re-query Jaeger with longer retention or a narrower window to obtain span-level error descriptions for the failing cart and frontend operations.
Review the cart deployment rollout at 00:18–00:20 from cluster change/audit history, since the pre-rollout ReplicaSet is gone.
